clue.text: Source of ice cream — indulgence, they say — somewhere in NYC

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the preceding words count for their sound

parts.note: Wall's is a British ice cream brand, and an indulgence is a treat; said together the two run into one place name

explanation.surface: Someone craving an ice cream treat while wandering around New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: Wall's is a long-standing British ice cream maker. Spoken quickly, Wall's treat merges into WALL STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street is the famous financial district in lower Manhattan, so it is a place located within New York City.

clue.text: Hesitate to bring food to table

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hold back or pause before acting
second meaning: serve diners, as restaurant staff do

explanation.surface: A diner unsure whether to start serving the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to delay or hold back and to serve customers at table, as waiters do.

clue.text: Delicate fabric is 'slightly irreplaceable'

indicators.note: slightly means only a small part of the following word is used, buried inside it

parts.note: four letters sit in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A precious piece of fine cloth that could hardly be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'slightly irreplaceable' look like a quoted joke, but slightly just asks for a small piece of the word: irrepLACEable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is an openwork textile made of fine threads, prized for its fragile, decorative quality.

clue.text: Incredibly, last union not offering protection

indicators.note: something incredible defies belief, hinting the following letters are wildly rearranged

parts.note: three words used letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A trade union, the last of its kind, fails to shield its members.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun cream is applied to skin to shield it from ultraviolet rays and burning, a form of protection.

clue.text: Oddly straying, priapic with lust and greed for sweet things

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters wander off, so only the even-placed ones remain

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of the word
lust and greed are two of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A lecherous character, straying from virtue, is also greedy for sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddly straying looks like a description of behaviour, but it removes the odd letters of priapic, leaving pRiApIc.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried grapes are naturally sugary, eaten as sweet treats and used in cakes and puddings.

clue.text: Ironing, perhaps at end of day

definitions.meaning: first meaning: making something flat or smooth, as pressing creases out of clothes does
second meaning: the time between late afternoon and night

explanation.surface: Doing the household pressing as the day draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironing reads as a chore, but it is an example of making even, the verb read as even-ing.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the close of the day, while the verbal form means smoothing or levelling, as an iron does.

clue.text: Trees where key limes regularly plucked

indicators.note: taking letters at a regular interval means every other one is picked out

parts.note: even-placed letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An orchard of trees where key limes are harvested regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elms are large deciduous broadleaf species common in parks and hedgerows, so they are a kind of tree.

clue.text: Novelist's novel, O, To Sell Trifle

indicators.note: novel means new, so the following letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
to trifle with something is to toy with it

explanation.surface: A writer's new book oddly titled O, To Sell Trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a noun, the writer's book, but here it is the adjective new and signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy was the Russian author of War and Peace and Anna Karenina, so he is a famous writer of fiction.

clue.text: Type of bridge in South America given means of support

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation
US is short for the United States of America
a regular retirement payment that supports someone financially

explanation.surface: A bridge somewhere in South America, held up by some form of support.
explanation.walkthrough: South America reads as one continent, but it splits into two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge whose deck hangs from cables slung between towers is a well-known engineering design, like the Golden Gate.

clue.text: Everyman's invested in … in smallest amounts of money to get carrots

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a cent is the smallest coin in many currencies
the setter, Everyman, speaking of himself: Everyman has becomes I have, shortened

explanation.surface: The setter puts a few pennies into something to earn rewards.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so Everyman's means I have, shortened to the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrots, as in carrot and stick, are rewards offered to encourage someone, which is what inducements are.

clue.text: Deer will suffice

definitions.meaning: second meaning: is enough, as in that'll do

explanation.surface: A hunter decides any deer at all will be good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Female deer are called by this plural noun, and the verb form means is sufficient, as in 'that does it'.

clue.text: Prepared a burrito; won't give you fish

indicators.note: food that is prepared is chopped and arranged, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the words used letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cook makes a Mexican wrap instead of the seafood dinner someone wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow variety is a freshwater species of the salmon family, prized by anglers and farmed for food.

clue.text: A Greek character with liquor and a nudge: careful what you're getting into here

definitions.text: careful what you're getting into here

parts.note: taken as written
a letter of the Greek alphabet
a spirit flavoured with juniper
taken as written
a prod or jab

explanation.surface: A tipsy Greek gets a warning nudge about the bargain they are entering.
explanation.walkthrough: A poke is an old word for a sack, so buying a pig in a poke is buying something unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a purchase made without inspection, so it is a warning to check before committing to a deal.

clue.text: And a pig ferociously eats tiny creature to become enormous beast

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece is placed within the other
acting ferociously suggests wild, violent disorder, so these letters are tossed about

parts.note: three words used letter for letter as fodder
an ant is a very small insect

explanation.surface: A savage pig devours a small creature and grows to monstrous size.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bear of China is a large mammal, the word giant itself signalling its great size.

clue.text: Technician: 'A spot of sepia? Not unerasable'

indicators.note: a spot is just a small portion, so only a stretch of the following run of words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the three words, ignoring the punctuation

explanation.surface: A technician complains that a spot of brown sepia ink cannot be erased.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside sePIA, continues through NOT and ends inside UNERasable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adjusts the strings of a keyboard instrument to correct pitch is a skilled specialist, a kind of technician.

clue.text: Eaves' droppers?

parts.note: surface reading: eavesdroppers, people secretly listening to others
setter's reading: things that drop from the eaves of a roof

explanation.walkthrough: Split with an apostrophe, the word for snoopers becomes things hanging and dripping from the roof edge in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen spikes form where meltwater drips from the overhanging edge of a roof, so they literally hang and drop from eaves.

clue.text: Eugene's Israelite carrying part of Torah

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it within, so the answer sits inside these words

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: An Israelite named Eugene carries a section of the holy scroll.
explanation.definitionFit: The Torah consists of the five books of Moses, the first of which tells of creation.

clue.text: Pontoons needing love, once renovated constantly

indicators.note: something renovated is rebuilt, so the remaining letters are reassembled
needing something means lacking it, so a piece must be taken away

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, a shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: Floating platforms in need of affection, once refurbished, are endlessly in use.
explanation.walkthrough: One O is dropped from the eight letters of the first word, and the seven left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without a break or pause means doing it all the time, so the two words share a sense.

clue.text: Ace succeeding, old stance, getting to green area

indicators.note: to succeed someone is to take their place, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: the way someone stands or holds their body
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A star player takes over from an old one and heads out onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In POSTURE the A takes the place of the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland where livestock graze is a stretch of green open country, often a field.

clue.text: In favour of U2's singer not getting any money

parts.note: pro means for, supporting
Bono is the lead vocalist of the Irish rock band U2

explanation.surface: Supporting the U2 frontman when he performs unpaid, as he does for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Bono is known for charity work, which makes the unpaid surface fit neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, short for for the public good, describes professional work done free of charge.

clue.text: Uplifting quiet time with love, quietly offering support

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: the sound made to ask for silence
T is the abbreviation for time
love means zero, as in a tennis score
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A quiet romantic moment gently lifts the spirits and gives emotional support.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces SH, T, NIL and P are put together and then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plinths are the solid bases on which statues or columns stand, so each is a kind of physical support.

clue.text: Religious symbol, where dancing or pants are not common

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and swap places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
ain't is a nonstandard, colloquial form of are not

explanation.surface: A sacred figure presides over a place where dancing and underwear are rarely seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Common here means vulgar or uneducated in speech, which is how ain't stands for are not.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint adopted as protector of a place, trade or person is venerated and acts as an emblem of faith.

clue.text: Confused vote delivering presidential power

indicators.note: a confused thing is jumbled, so the next word's letters come out in another order

parts.note: used letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A muddled election result hands authority to the president.
explanation.definitionFit: A US president can reject a bill passed by Congress, an authority to block legislation.

clue.text: Regularly in bedrooms, making love

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Lovemaking happening routinely in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of desire, and the name also stands for romantic or sexual passion.

clue.text: Sister's outspoken; not at all!

indicators.note: something spoken out is heard, so the word before it counts for its sound

parts.note: a sister is a member of a religious order

explanation.surface: A nun speaks her mind, firmly refusing with an indignant no.
explanation.walkthrough: Outspoken looks like a description of the sister's character, but it signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, as in none the wiser, the word means to no degree whatsoever.

clue.text: One who sells essence of rum, mixed with ice or neat

indicators.note: a mixed drink has its ingredients stirred together, so these letters are combined in a new order
the essence of something is its heart, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the word
three words used letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A barman sells rum either on the rocks or straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice or neat are the two ways of serving a spirit, which keeps the drinks picture going.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer conducts public sales, taking bids and selling goods to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Where you can see Asia's grandest royal abode, primarily?

definitions.text: Where you can see Asia's grandest royal abode, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A question about where to view the finest royal palace in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the Taj Mahal, a royal mausoleum, stands in this Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city on the Yamuna is home to the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort, famous Mughal monuments.

clue.text: Numbers overwhelm these whizzes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: feelings, which things that numb, such as anaesthetics, suppress
second meaning: stars or prodigies who cause a stir

explanation.walkthrough: Numbers wants to mean figures, as if maths swamps the gifted; read it as numb-ers, things that deaden feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical feelings are dulled by numbing agents, and dazzling performers who cause excitement are hits or prodigies.
